sections.h2: Does a Florida homeowner owe tax on profit from selling a house?
sections.html:
Possibly, but a federal exclusion wipes out most or all of the profit for many sellers of a main residence. A single filer can shield $250,000 of profit, and a married couple filing together can shield $500,000, as long as two tests are passed. The figure applies to a Florida house exactly as it would to a house anywhere else in the country.

What Florida adds is local paperwork around the transfer: the deed, the stamp tax collected at recording, and the county's reassessment of the property for the next owner. Those pieces are covered after the federal rules below.

sections.h2: Which two tests unlock the exclusion?
sections.html:
You need to pass an ownership test and a use test inside the five years that end on the closing date. Each test asks for 24 months, and the months need not be consecutive. The IRS also says the two tests may be satisfied in different two-year stretches, provided both land in that five-year window.

  • Ownership: you or your spouse held title for two years out of the five.
  • Use: the house was your residence for two years out of the five, and on a joint return both spouses must pass this one.
  • Prior sale: the break is generally unavailable if you claimed it on a different house during the two years before this closing.

Publication 523, the IRS guide to selling a home, has the worksheets, the partial exclusions for early moves, and the exceptions to the two-year rule. Read it before you assume that eighteen months is enough.

sections.h2: How is the taxable profit figured when the exclusion falls short?
sections.html:
Take the price you realize at closing and subtract your adjusted basis. Basis starts with your cost and rises with permanent improvements such as a new roof or an added bedroom. It falls with items like depreciation and insurance payments for casualty losses. Hold on to old closing statements and contractor receipts, because they are your proof.

Holding period decides the label. Profit on property you held longer than a year is long-term and eligible for the lower rate bands. Anything held a year or less is short-term and is taxed like wages. If the house came to you by inheritance or gift, the IRS sends you to Publication 551 for basis, which matters to a Florida family clearing out a relative's home.

A loss on a personal residence cannot be deducted. Losses on investment property are different: they offset gains, and up to $3,000 of any excess ($1,500 for married filing separately) reduces other income each year, with the balance carried forward.

sections.h2: What federal rates apply to profit above the exclusion?
sections.html:
Most net long-term gain falls into a 0%, 15% or 20% band set by taxable income, and the IRS prints different bands for each filing status. The table copies the bands the IRS shows for tax years starting in 2025. Thresholds move annually, so look at the IRS page for the year of your closing.

IRS long-term gain bands for tax years beginning in 2025
RateSingle filerJoint return
0%Income up to $48,350Income up to $96,700
15%$48,350 to $533,400$96,700 to $600,050
20%Income above the 15% bandIncome above the 15% band

Two extra items can raise the bill. A 25% ceiling applies to the unrecaptured section 1250 slice of gain, which arises when depreciation was claimed on a home office or rental space. Sellers with large investment income may also face a separate surtax that the IRS describes on Topic 559.

sections.h2: Must a fully excluded sale still go on the return?
sections.html:
It must if the closing agent sends you a Form 1099-S. The IRS says to report the sale in that case even though no tax results. If the gain is larger than your exclusion, report it too, on the Form 8949 and Schedule D pair that the IRS names for this.

Keep a folder for the sale: the purchase closing statement, improvement receipts, the new settlement statement and any 1099-S. A tax preparer can work from those papers in minutes, and a missing receipt can leave a legitimate improvement out of your basis.

Title companies in Florida normally prepare the 1099-S from the settlement statement. Ask your closing agent before you sign whether one will be filed in your name. Sellers with a taxable gain may also owe estimated payments during the year, which Publication 505 explains.

sections.h2: Are there timing rules for military sellers and installment sales?
sections.html:
Yes. A service member, Foreign Service officer or intelligence community employee on qualified extended duty may elect to freeze the five-year clock for as long as ten years. Extended duty means more than 90 days or an open-ended assignment, at a post 50 or more miles from the home or in government quarters under orders. Many Florida owners near bases and ports fit this description.

A sale where the buyer pays across later years counts as an installment sale, and the IRS tells sellers to use installment reporting unless they opt out. The home sale exclusion still applies to the part you can exclude. Look at Publication 537 and Form 6252 for the mechanics.

sections.h2: What Florida deed and reassessment rules touch the sale?
sections.html:
Florida taxes the deed at seventy cents on each $100 of price in every county except Miami-Dade, where the printed charge is 60 cents plus a surtax. That surtax is skipped for a paper conveying only a single-family dwelling. Every party to the deed is liable, whoever the contract says will pay. The clerk takes payment when the deed goes on record.

  • An estate's personal representative who deeds property under a probated will is listed as not taxable.
  • A spousal homestead deed whose only consideration is a mortgage is exempt, and so is a divorce deed for the marital home.
  • One Department advisement found a lady bird deed outside the stamp tax on the facts it described, so ask a Florida attorney before relying on that.

For the buyer, the new owner's assessment resets to full just value, ending the old Save Our Homes cap. Florida also hands residential buyers a written tax disclosure, which tells them not to assume your current bill will carry over. A homestead owner who plans to buy again should look at portability, which the Department says requires the new homestead to be established inside a three-year window that is counted from the year the old homestead was abandoned, with Form DR-501T filed alongside the DR-501 by March 1. These steps change the buyer's cost, not your gain.

faqs.q: Does the federal exclusion work the same way for a Florida home?
faqs.a: Yes. The $250,000 and $500,000 limits come from federal tax law and apply to a main home anywhere in the country. Florida does not change the ownership and use tests, though the deed and county records follow Florida procedure.

faqs.q: How many months must I live in the house before selling?
faqs.a: Twenty-four months of residence and twenty-four months of ownership, both inside the five years ending at closing. The months need not be consecutive, and the two tests may be met in different two-year periods.

faqs.q: Can I take the exclusion again soon after another sale?
faqs.a: Generally not. The IRS says you usually cannot if you excluded profit on another house during the two years before this closing. Publication 523 lists exceptions.

faqs.q: I will owe nothing. Do I still tell the IRS?
faqs.a: If a Form 1099-S arrives, yes. The IRS wants it reported even if every dollar of gain is excludable, and also when part of the gain is taxable.
Your purchase cost plus lasting improvements, reduced by depreciation and insurance reimbursements for casualty losses. Inherited or gifted homes follow different basis rules in IRS Publication 551.
